For a.e. p ∈ B', (b) gives c p_1 = toReal(H(p)) ≥ 0, while c p_1 < 0; so a.e. p lies outside B', i.e. B' is Lebesgue-null (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem), a contradiction. Hence c ≥ 0.

By Tonelli on the product of intervals (Measure.prod_restrict, lintegral_prod), ∫_{Sq(s')} ofReal(c p_1) dp = ∫_{(1−s',1+s')} ofReal(ct)·λ((−s', s')) dt = ofReal(2s')·∫_{(1−s',1+s')} ofReal(ct) dt. Since t ↦ ct is continuous, hence integrable on the bounded interval, and nonnegative there (c ≥ 0 and t > 1 − s' ≥ 7/8 > 0), ∫_{(1−s',1+s')} ofReal(ct) dt = ofReal(∫_{1−s'}^{1+s'} ct dt) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal) = ofReal(c·((1 + s')² − (1 − s')²)/2) = ofReal(2cs') (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, integral_id). Hence I(s') = ofReal(2s')·ofReal(2cs') = ofReal(4c)·ofReal(s'²) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, c ≥ 0).
4. (c = m.) For 0 < s' ≤ s/8, ofReal(s'²) is neither 0 nor ∞, so I(s')/ofReal(s'²) = ofReal(4c) (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel_right). Since (0, s/8] ∈ 𝓝[>]0 (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT, s/8 > 0), the function s' ↦ I(s')/ofReal(s'²) is eventually equal to the constant ofReal(4c) along 𝓝[>]0, hence tends to ofReal(4c) (tendsto_const_nhds.congr').
